subject: english-literature
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What does Priestley imply by having each family member tied to the same girl?
options: That the actions of individuals combine to cause real harm to others
That only Mr Birling is to blame
questions.explain: The chain of linked actions shows how everyone's choices contributed to Eva's downfall, reinforcing collective responsibility.

questions.q: What central message does Inspector Goole deliver about society?
options: That the rich deserve their wealth
That "we are members of one body" and responsible for one another
That the law solves all problems
questions.explain: The Inspector argues people are responsible for each other, the play's theme of social responsibility.

questions.q: How does Sheila change in her attitude during the Inspector's interrogation?
options: She accepts responsibility and warns the others not to build a "wall"
She becomes more like her father
questions.explain: Sheila grows mature and remorseful, urging her family not to pretend the Inspector cannot touch them.

questions.q: Mr Birling can be seen to represent which political viewpoint?
questions.explain: Birling champions individual profit and dismisses community, embodying capitalist values Priestley critiques.

questions.q: What does Mr Birling hope his daughter's engagement to Gerald will bring his business?
options: Closer ties and lower costs with Crofts Limited, a rival firm
questions.explain: Birling hopes the marriage will join his firm with Gerald's family's company, Crofts Limited, benefiting both.

questions.q: The play is set in 1912 but was written in 1945. What does Priestley use this gap to comment on?
options: The two World Wars and the need for social change
questions.explain: Writing after two world wars, Priestley contrasts Birling's complacency with the lessons of conflict.

questions.q: How was Eric Birling involved with Eva Smith?
options: He fathered her unborn child and stole money to support her
He reported her to his father
questions.explain: Eric had a relationship with Eva, got her pregnant, and took money from the firm to help her.

questions.q: What is the name of the young woman whose death the Inspector investigates?
questions.explain: The dead girl is Eva Smith, who also went by the name Daisy Renton.

questions.q: How did Mrs Birling contribute to Eva Smith's death?
options: She sacked her from a shop
She used her influence to deny Eva help from a charity
She gave her too much money
questions.explain: As head of a charity, Mrs Birling refused the pregnant Eva assistance and blamed the father.

questions.q: In An Inspector Calls, in which English city is the play set?
options: The fictional industrial city of Brumley
questions.explain: Priestley sets the play in the fictional industrial Midlands city of Brumley in 1912.

questions.q: Which characters are most changed by the Inspector's visit?
options: Sheila and Eric, the younger generation
questions.explain: The younger Birlings accept their guilt, while their parents largely refuse to change.

questions.q: What relationship did Gerald Croft have with Daisy Renton?
options: He kept her as his mistress for a time
questions.explain: Gerald had an affair with Daisy Renton, keeping her for several months before ending it.

questions.q: Why did Mr Birling first cause harm to Eva Smith?
options: He sacked her for asking for higher wages
He reported her to the Inspector
questions.explain: Birling dismissed Eva from his factory for leading a request for a pay rise.

questions.q: How does the play present the theme of generational divide?
options: The old and young agree on everything
The younger Birlings learn from events while the older ones cling to their views
questions.explain: Sheila and Eric absorb the lesson of responsibility, but Mr and Mrs Birling refuse to change, highlighting a generational split.

questions.q: What does Gerald discover that makes the family question whether Goole was a real inspector?
options: That the Inspector was a Birling relative
That the local police have no officer named Goole
questions.explain: Gerald learns from a police contact that there is no Inspector Goole on the force, casting doubt on the whole visit.

questions.q: How was Sheila Birling responsible for Eva Smith's misfortune?
options: She reported her to the police
She had Eva dismissed from a shop out of jealousy
questions.explain: Sheila got Eva sacked from Milwards in a fit of jealous temper.

questions.q: In An Inspector Calls, what is the occasion at the Birling household when the play opens?
questions.explain: The family is celebrating the engagement of Sheila Birling to Gerald Croft.

questions.q: What does Inspector Goole warn will happen if people do not learn the lesson of responsibility?
options: They will be taught it "in fire and blood and anguish"
questions.explain: His final speech warns that ignoring social responsibility leads to suffering "in fire and blood and anguish".

questions.q: How does Eric's drinking feature in the play's exploration of his character?
options: It is praised by Mr Birling
It makes him the family hero
It reveals a hidden problem and his reckless behaviour towards Eva
questions.explain: Eric's heavy drinking, which his parents had overlooked, is tied to his exploitation of Eva and his troubled conduct.

questions.q: What does the name "Goole" suggest about the Inspector's symbolic role?
options: That he is ghostly or otherworldly, like a moral conscience
That he is related to the Birlings
That he is a policeman of high rank
questions.explain: "Goole" echoes "ghoul", hinting the Inspector is a supernatural or moral force rather than an ordinary policeman.

questions.q: What unsettling twist occurs at the very end of the play?
options: A phone call announces a real inspector is coming to investigate a girl's death
questions.explain: After doubting Goole was real, the family learns a girl has died and a police inspector is on his way.

questions.q: How does Mrs Birling's response to the Inspector reveal her prejudice?
options: She looks down on Eva as a girl of a lower class undeserving of help
questions.explain: Mrs Birling dismisses Eva as a member of the lower classes and refuses her charity, exposing her snobbery.
